may they rest in peace. mission sunday 2026 – theme: one in christ – united in mission world mission sunday is the holy father’s annual appeal for spiritual and financial support so that the life-giving work of overseas mission and missionaries can continue. it always falls on the second last sunday in october, meaning this year it will be celebrated over the weekend of sunday 18th october . “right now, missionaries desperately need your help. in many poorer parishes in africa, asia , and latin america missionaries are serving on the front line. they already do so much, walking hand-in-hand with margina lised communities, long before and after any emergency. you can show missionaries you care by supporting world mission sunday. your prayers and generosity will change lives.” world mission sunday collections take place in every single parish where the church is present. this includes not only ireland and europe, but also in poorer parishes in developing countries. it is a moment of universal solidarity when each member of the church family, regardless of location or background, play their part in supporting each other. this is what makes it such a special celebration. / 01 5529448. parish partnership name throughout the diocese parishes are being called to come together in new forms. grouping, cluster, amalgamation of parishes are the way ahead for the diocese that is reduced in priests to service local areas. we are privileged that the parish of saggart, rathcoole, brittas and the parish of newcastle have been working together for many years. a shared parish pastoral council and finance committee has been in place for a number of years showing a shared interest and cooperation between the ‘four districts’. we have been invited to discern a common name that has a resonance throughout the area. a number of matters are considered to be significant in relation to parish partnership patron names. generally, a parish partnership name should: 1. have a unifying character, avoiding the name of any one parish/church in the partnership; 2. be appropriate to the partnership mission or connect with a tradition of faith in the areae.g. a local saint’s name or the name of a local monastery or well; 3. be discerned appropriately by people of all of the parishes in the partnership; 4. not be already in use by another parish partnership in the archdiocese. one suggestion raised recently was “mo sacra” a saint from the 7th century who set up a monastery in what is currently saggart cemetery. st brigid’s well in rathcoole, st. finian’s well in newcastle are other names. have you any thoughts or suggestions on a name that could be used. ‘saggart’ was also a suggestion given. aware – support & self care groups if you or those with whom you work wish to connect with people in relation to your mental we llbeing, consider using aware’s phone-in and zoom support and self-care groups, support line or support mail. for more information, visit

removed_lines: newman was a leading intellectual and writer of 19th century england who famously converted to catholicism, founded what later became university college dublin, built university church on st stephen’s green and is known for his prayerful concern for people’s spiritual welfare and his love for the poor in birmingham. newman points out that sometimes we are led to think that we ought to be useful on a large scale and to move away from our usual “line of life”. but he tells us that this should not be the case. “we need not give up our usual manner of life, in order to serve god and that “that the most humble and quietest station is acceptable to him, if improved duly.” in one of his more famous quotations, saint john henry wrote: “in a higher world it is otherwise but here below to live is to change and to be perfect is to change often .” i think this perfectly describes his pragmatic approach to life and to ministry.

i have nothing of th at high perfection which belongs to the writings of saints . but what i trust that i may claim all through what i have written, is this, —an honest intention, an absence of private ends, a temper of obedience, a willingness to be corrected, a dread of error, a desire to serve holy church , and, through divine mercy, a fair measure of success .” newman advocated a middle course – via media – advocating a reasoned approach to the various challenges that he faced.
